messages:
alex: Anyone else seeing a reconnect storm from SSE clients right after token rotation? Console shows lots of 'new' sessions and quota spikes even though clients claim they were trying to resume. https://console/internal/streams/trace/abcd
maria: yup, I pulled traces. Proxy returns 401 for a short window during rotation, clients retry -> new session creation. But the resume flow sometimes arrives a few ms later, so billing counts both.
jamal: logs: proxy sets connection as CLOSED on 401 then resume arrives with no Resume-Id header so the backend treats it as a fresh stream. Billing uses session-start event.
alex: example headers from a failing resume:
```
GET /sse/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <rotated-token>
Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: redwood-sse-v1
# missing: Resume-Id: 12345
```

sasha: if resume arrives without Resume-Id we have two choices: 1) make proxy do idempotency by matching client IP+last-offset (messy), or 2) add a short auth-grace window where previous token version is accepted so proxy never closes the old connection.
tian: the auth token rotation TTL is currently 30s sliding, but rotation happens aggressively during deploys. If token version increments while streaming, clients are forced to re-auth. We could add a 5s overlap grace on token verification.
maria: grace window is easiest short-term. Longer-term we should require clients to include Resume-Id when resuming and have proxy preserve session mapping for X seconds. But mobile/third-party clients may not be updated.
jamal: also seeing a telemetry gap: console shows two sessions but traces don't link them. We need a resume.link_id or token-version in traces so Ops can correlate.
sasha: proposal: Add header `Resume-Id` on resume handshake and `X-Token-Version` on all stream traffic. On proxy, when a resume handshake arrives, check Resume-Id; if present, mark session as resumed and do NOT emit billing event for the new connection. If absent, still try a soft-match for 100ms before emitting billing.
alex: that soft-match window is good but risky: what if a malicious actor replays a resume? But Resume-Id + short TTL should be fine.
tian: new metrics we should emit: `resume_attempts`, `resume_success`, `resume_late_new_session`, `auth_rotation_rejects`, `resume_softmatches`. Add these to the console and wire alerts when resume_late_new_session > 1% in 5m.
maria: I'll add a dashboard tile that shows per-tenant resume success rate, and annotate deploy windows so we can correlate spikes.
jamal: for billing, add a temporary flag `suppress-billing-on-potential-resume` (admin-only) that prevents immediate charge on new session if a resume attempt appears within 500ms in traces. We can enable this for affected tenants while we roll this out.
sasha: API debate: Should the proxy accept previous token versions automatically (grace) or should rotation be responsibility of token issuer to sign both versions? Prefers proxy-side grace because it's simpler to roll out.
tian: agree. Implement grace for 5s and require Resume-Id for long-term fix.
alex: I'll open an RFC and a small patch: proxy will accept previous token for 5s and log token-version pair; add Resume-Id header handling and new metrics. Rollout plan: canary on prod-1 for 15m, monitor resume_success and billing delta.
deploy-bot: Canary deployed: proxy v3.12.4-canary on cluster prod-1, change-id=proxy-auth-grace-3421. Watch metrics: resumes, billing, new_connection_rate.
maria: started dashboard PR (#451) adding resume metrics + annotation.
jamal: I'll gate the billing suppress flag behind a feature toggle and keep it off by default. Will prepare migration notes for finance.
sasha: client SDKs need a small patch to send Resume-Id on reconnect. I'll send notify to devex for SDK releases.
alex: next steps: (1) implement 5s grace + Resume-Id handling in proxy (2) add new metrics and console tiles (maria) (3) roll canary, watch for billing delta (jamal) (4) ship SDK update to include Resume-Id (sasha).
alex: thanks, everyone. If we see any unexpected increases in latency or new error classes during canary, ping #oncall immediately. :thumbsup:
